members.name: Qinqin Lin
members.bio:
Qinqin Lin is a lecturer in the Department of Marine Fisheries Science and Technology at Shanghai Ocean University. Her research examines pelagic fish population dynamics and how fishing and climate change affect marine ecosystems. She develops ecosystem models to support ecosystem-based fisheries management, with a focus on tropical Pacific food webs and tuna fisheries.

She earned her PhD at Shanghai Ocean University in 2022 and completed postdoctoral research there from 2022 to 2024. She was a visiting scholar at the University of Maine in 2021–2022. Her work also supports China’s participation in the Inter-American Tropical Tuna Commission (IATTC).
members.photo_alt: Qinqin Lin at a fisheries meeting

hero.summary: I study pelagic fish population dynamics, tropical Pacific food webs, and how fishing and climate change affect marine ecosystems.

members.name: Xin Cheng
members.bio: Xin Cheng is a postdoctoral researcher at the Oceanic Fisheries Ecosystem Laboratory, Shanghai Ocean University. Her research uses artificial intelligence and vessel-tracking data to study fishing-vessel behaviour and tuna fleet dynamics. She develops deep learning methods for vessel classification and examines how fishing activity varies across regions and over time. Her recent work also assesses the quality of Automatic Identification System (AIS) data to support fisheries monitoring and management.

hero.summary: I use artificial intelligence and vessel-tracking data to study fishing-vessel behaviour, tuna fleets, and the quality of AIS data.

members.name: Sisong Dong
members.bio: Sisong Dong is a postdoctoral researcher at the Oceanic Fisheries Ecosystem Laboratory, Shanghai Ocean University. His research focuses on stock assessment for tuna and coastal marine species, using quantitative population models to inform fisheries management.
members.photo_alt: Road bicycle beside a tree-lined road

hero.summary: I work on stock assessment for tuna and coastal marine species, using quantitative population models to inform fisheries management.

members.name: Dongqi Lu
members.bio:
Dongqi Lu is a PhD student in Aquaculture at Shanghai Ocean University. His research focuses on spatial variation in the growth of South Pacific albacore tuna and the factors that drive these differences. He combines age and growth analysis with genetic and genomic evidence to study population structure and improve the biological information used in tuna stock assessments.

His work draws on port sampling, biological observations from tuna longline surveys, and fishery logbook and observer data. He also contributes to observer training and technical reporting for regional fisheries management organisations.
members.photo_alt: Dongqi Lu beside the Sydney Opera House

hero.summary: I study how South Pacific albacore grow, combining age and growth analysis with genetic and genomic evidence to understand population structure.

members.name: Hongyu Lin
members.photo_alt: A cat resting on a sofa, chosen by Hongyu Lin for his profile
members.bio:
Hongyu Lin is a PhD student at Shanghai Ocean University working on fisheries stock assessment and spatiotemporal modelling. His research examines tuna population dynamics under climate variability and change, with particular attention to the El Niño–Southern Oscillation (ENSO). He also works on catch-per-unit-effort (CPUE) standardisation and management strategy evaluation.

His work spans the Pacific and Atlantic oceans, including waters managed by multiple regional fisheries management organisations. He received China Scholarship Council (CSC) funding for a one-year joint doctoral research placement at the University of Washington in Seattle, USA.

hero.summary: I study tuna population dynamics under climate variability, with a focus on stock assessment, spatiotemporal modelling, and fisheries management.

members.name: Mingfeng Jiang
members.bio:
Mingfeng Jiang is a PhD student in Fisheries Resources at Shanghai Ocean University, supervised by Professor Fan Zhang. After studying civil engineering as an undergraduate, he moved into marine fisheries science for his master’s and doctoral studies.

His research focuses on cephalopod population dynamics and stock assessment, particularly jumbo squid in the southeast Pacific. He develops models that account for death after spawning and examines how ENSO shapes squid migration and reproduction. He also evaluates seasonal fishing closures as a means of conserving oceanic squid. He received a 2026 National Scholarship.
members.photo_alt: Mingfeng Jiang beside a lake in winter

hero.summary: I study jumbo squid population dynamics and stock assessment, including death after spawning, ENSO, and seasonal fishing closures.

members.name: Xiaoci Wu
members.bio:
Xiaoci Wu is a PhD student at Shanghai Ocean University working in fisheries oceanography and stock assessment. His research examines how climate change and mesoscale ocean processes shape cephalopod distributions and population dynamics.

He has contributed to projects supported by the Shanghai Natural Science Foundation and open research funds from key laboratories in offshore fisheries development and satellite ocean environment dynamics. His work includes processing fisheries and ocean environmental data, analysing the spatial and temporal patterns of fishing grounds, and building habitat suitability models.

He also participated in a comprehensive high-seas fisheries survey in the western and central Pacific, spending about six weeks at sea. Over the past three years, he has published four first-authored papers in SCI-indexed journals.

members.name: Junyi Zhang
members.bio:
Junyi Zhang is a PhD student at Shanghai Ocean University working in fisheries ecology and fisheries oceanography. His research examines how climate change affects habitat suitability and the spatial and temporal distribution of fishery resources. He also studies fish community responses to environmental change and interactions among species, alongside food-web structure and trophic relationships in marine ecosystems.

Over the past three years, he has published two first-authored papers in SCI-indexed journals and two first-authored papers in journals indexed by the Chinese Science Citation Database (CSCD).

members.name: Runze Wang
members.bio:
Runze Wang is a master’s student at Shanghai Ocean University working on fisheries stock assessment. His research focuses on how model uncertainty is identified and specified in tuna assessments, and how modelling choices and institutional practices influence the assessment process.

As a co-first author of a study published in Fish and Fisheries, he reviewed 133 stock assessments covering seven major commercial tuna species across five regional fisheries management organisations. This work compares uncertainty specifications among organisations and provides guidance for making assessments more consistent and transparent.

hero.summary: I study uncertainty in tuna stock assessments: how it is identified, specified, and shaped by modelling choices and institutional practices.

members.name: Shuang Ma
members.photo_alt: A game character holding a plush creature, chosen by Shuang Ma for this profile
members.bio:
I’m a graduate student slowly being domesticated by research. Academic papers by day, fan works by night. I can track fishing vessels across the Pacific with AIS, yet often can’t locate my own research direction.

I have a knack for turning a passing obsession into a three-year project. My hobbies form unsupervised clusters. My state of mind follows a random walk, my idealism converges intermittently, and deadlines keep closing in.

members.name: Weiguo Li
members.photo_alt: Hands on a plasma globe, chosen by Weiguo Li for his profile
members.bio:
I’m a master’s student trying to make sense of fish population dynamics, fisheries stock assessment, and why SPiCT is refusing to run yet again. Most days, I bounce between papers, data, code, and prior distributions. I’m committed to getting models to converge, and equally committed to figuring out why they converged the way they did.

I study fish in the sea and tinker with models on my computer. Research is a long and winding road, but as long as the code still runs, there’s still hope.

一个试图搞懂鱼类种群动态、渔业资源评估，以及 SPiCT 为什么又跑不出来的研究生。日常在文献、数据、代码和先验分布之间反复横跳，致力于让模型收敛，也致力于弄明白它为什么这样收敛。

研究海里的鱼，折腾电脑里的模型。科研之路道阻且长，但只要代码还能运行，生活就还有希望。

hero.summary: I’m trying to make sense of fish population dynamics, fisheries stock assessment, and why SPiCT is refusing to run yet again.

members.name: Xianglong Yan
members.bio:
Xianglong Yan is a master’s student at Shanghai Ocean University, which he joined in September 2026 after completing his undergraduate studies at Dalian Ocean University. His research interests centre on fish feeding ecology and coastal ecosystems.

His undergraduate thesis used carbon and nitrogen stable isotopes to investigate the feeding ecology of black rockfish in the Zhuanghe offshore wind farm area. His training also includes Ecopath ecosystem modelling and fish growth analysis, alongside practical work on fish behaviour and artificial reef design.

hero.summary: I study fish feeding ecology and coastal ecosystems, with training in stable isotopes, Ecopath modelling, and fish growth analysis.
